title: Finite uniform cohomology bound for quasi-coherent sheaves on a qcqs algebraic space
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$ with its small etale structure sheaf $\mathcal O_X$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Assume $X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated: every open cover of $|X|$ has a finite subcover and its absolute diagonal is quasi-compact. There exists an integer $C\geq1$, depending only on $X$, such that for every quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $M$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module] and every integer $q\geq C$, one has $H^q(X_{\mathrm{et}},M_{ab})=0$. Here $M_{ab}$ is the underlying abelian sheaf, and $H^q(X_{\mathrm{et}},-)$ is the right derived functor of abelian-sheaf global sections [def-sp-left-exact-additive], computed on injective resolutions [def-sp-injective-resolutions]; global sections are families of sections compatible with every restriction on the small etale site, whether or not that site has a final object. No dimension bound, Noetherian assumption or finite-generation condition on $M$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 072C, label lemma-vanishing-quasi-separated, existence of the finite atlas data and the final vanishing assertion; enlarge its bound max(d_p+p) to at least 1.

proof.text: Choose an affine surjective etale atlas $f:U\to X$ by [lem-sfb-qc-space-affine-etale-atlas]. Apply [lem-sfb-space-qc-etale-fibre-bound] and enlarge its bound to an integer $d\geq1$. Thus every geometric fibre of $f$ has at most $d$ points. These choices depend on $X$, not on a module.

source.place: Tag 072C, first paragraph: affine atlas and universally bounded fibres.

proof.text: For $p\geq0$ form the ordered distinct-tuple scheme $W_p$ with $p+1$ factors. By [lem-sfb-etale-atlas-distinct-tuple-geometry] it is quasi-compact and separated. The same result for two factors identifies the diagonal of $f$ with the closed pairwise equality locus, so $f$ is separated. A geometric point of $W_p$ over $\bar x$ is a tuple of $p+1$ distinct points of $U_{\bar x}$; consequently $W_p=\varnothing$ for $p\geq d$. Indeed any point of a nonempty scheme has a geometric representative, which would contradict $p+1>d$.

source.place: Tag 072C, first paragraph and the vanishing of configurations for p at least d; use p+1 in the existing tuple-geometry indexing.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-alternating-sign-cohomology-spectral] to $f$. It supplies $Q_p=W_p/\mathfrak S_{p+1}$, the surjective etale quotient atlas, and $g_p:Q_p\to X$. By [lem-sfb-free-finite-space-quotient-separated], applied over the base $S$ with $W=W_p$ (absolutely separated by step 2) and $G=\mathfrak S_{p+1}$ acting over $X$, hence over $S$, $Q_p$ is separated in the absolute sense. Freeness on scheme tests holds: a $T$-point of $W_p$ fixed by $\sigma\neq1$ on a nonempty open and closed part of $T$ would have two equal coordinates there, so that part would map into an equality locus, which $W_p$ avoids. It is quasi-compact: the inverse images of an open cover under the continuous surjection $|W_p|\to|Q_p|$ cover the quasi-compact $W_p$, hence a finite subfamily covers $Q_p$; continuity is the atlas-topology definition [def-a1-space-point-topology]. For each of the finitely many $0\leq p<d$, choose an affine surjective etale $V_p\to Q_p$ and a geometric fibre bound $d_p\geq1$ by [lem-sfb-qc-space-affine-etale-atlas, lem-sfb-space-qc-etale-fibre-bound]. The second lemma applies since the diagonal is quasi-compact: on any scheme test its inverse image of an affine is a closed affine subscheme by [def-weil-closed-immersion]; a finite affine cover gives quasi-compact inverse images of quasi-compact opens. If $W_p$ is empty, its surjective quotient is empty too. All these choices are independent of the module.

source.place: Tag 072C, first paragraph: separated unordered configurations and affine atlases; correct the printed V_p to W_p typo to V_p to U_p (our Q_p).

proof.text: Fix a quasi-coherent $M$. In the spectral sequence the coefficient on $Q_p$ is $N_p=g_p^*M\otimes_{\mathbf Z}L_p$, whose underlying abelian sheaf is $g_p^{-1}M_{ab}\otimes_{\mathbf Z}L_p$. This is quasi-coherent by the local presentation definition [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]: etale restriction preserves its local presentation, and on the etale cover trivializing $L_p$ the tensor is simply the restricted module itself. The local trivialization comes from [lem-sfb-space-alternating-sign-cohomology-spectral]. This is the elementary argument of Tag 072A, not a further lemma. Apply [lem-sfb-separated-space-atlas-cohomology-bound] to the quasi-compact separated $Q_p$, its affine atlas $V_p$ and its bound $d_p$. For $p<d$ it gives $E_1^{p,q}=0$ whenever $q\geq d_p$. For $p\geq d$, $Q_p$ is empty and its sheaf cohomology is zero in every degree: the empty covering forces every abelian sheaf to be zero.

source.place: Tags 072C, last paragraph, 072A (local triviality argument), and 072B (separated-space vanishing).

proof.text: Set $C=\max(1,\max_{0\leq p<d}(p+d_p))$, a finite integer independent of $M$. For $n\geq C$ and $p+q=n$ in the first quadrant, either $p\geq d$ or $q=n-p\geq C-p\geq d_p$. Thus every $E_1$ entry on total degree $n$ is zero. Zero entries remain zero on all later pages since the next entry is a subquotient of the previous one. The finite abutment filtration supplied by [lem-sfb-space-alternating-sign-cohomology-spectral] therefore has zero successive quotients. Starting with $F^{n+1}=0$ and proceeding down to $F^0$ gives $H^n(X_{\mathrm{et}},M_{ab})=0$. Since $C\geq1$, this covers every integer degree in the statement.

source.place: Tag 072C, final sentence: the finite diagonal and finite-filtration argument, with the bound enlarged to at least 1.
